value.body: A dialysis technologist runs haemodialysis sessions for people whose kidneys no longer work well, under a nephrologist's supervision. Employers include hospitals, standalone dialysis centres and public-private dialysis programmes. A typical day involves preparing machines, connecting and monitoring patients through sessions of several hours, and cleaning and maintaining equipment.

items.label: Works under
items.value: A nephrologist and dialysis nurse in charge

items.label: Regulation
items.value: Allied health professions fall under the NCAHP Act, 2021

items.label: Patients served under PMNDP
items.note: ~3.4 crore dialysis sessions in total since launch

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Graduates usually join a hospital or dialysis centre as a technologist after an internship during the degree. Shift work, including early mornings, is common because centres run several sessions a day.

value.title: At a glance
items: Patients often come several times a week, so technologists build long-term relationships with them.
Next roles: senior technologist, dialysis unit in-charge, trainer.
